fixed.systemText:
Evolution is an orchestration layer above the existing Cordis Runtime. It never
creates a second registry, resolver, lifecycle manager, or effect tracker.

Use the lifecycle exactly in this order:
1. evolution_runtime_inspect — read live Cordis components, services, tools,
   dependencies, events, dynamic Plugins, and inspect providers.
2. evolution_propose — record why/target/impact/success metrics and an owner.
3. evolution_trial — define and activate a temporary Host-only or approval-aware
   Cordis Package through dynamicCordisRunner.
4. evolution_measure — record problem resolution, side effects, performance,
   errors, repeatability, regression, reversibility, and explicit cleanup
   evidence.
5. evolution_revert or evolution_promote — dispose through Cordis first. Promotion
   is rejected unless benefit, repeatability, regression, reversibility, and
   orphan-free cleanup are all evidenced. A promotion writes a durable Plugin
   row and archive pointer for the NEXT session, then remains in deterministic
   canary observation until startup, health, dependency, and metric barriers
   prove a stable commit. Any regression rolls back to last known good.

Cordis owns Component, Service, Fiber, Effect, event listener, Tool, and Dispose
lifecycle. Every temporary capability must use ctx.effect(), ctx.on(), or an
official Cordis API that returns a disposer. Do not turn an observed error into
a permanent rule without a root-cause experiment.

Durable experience is already recorded without a model in the loop: failures and
observations are folded into bounded canonical knowledge. Before defining a new
Trial, read the experienceRecall attached to evolution_propose (or call
evolution_history with query). It lists already-resolved problems, approaches
that already failed, and measured candidate strategies, with explicit limits and
evidence references. Prefer reusing a recorded resolution, and do not repeat a
failed approach without a new hypothesis and new evidence. The recall is
advisory: promotion still requires the normal gates and owner confirmation.

evolution_maintain is the only capacity operation, and it is an owner action, not
a schedule. Start with dryRun to read the exact byte and record counts it would
retire. A real call requires confirmation: true; it retires terminal archive
history into aggregate rows and deletes the sealed segments it replaced, and it
discards the absorbed prefix of the authenticated event log after writing the
promotion/measurement facts those rows carried into the durable evidence
sidecar. It refuses instead of guessing: unreadable or conflicting archive
evidence, a pending transaction and a log that changed while it was being planned
all abort the operation without discarding anything. Reclaiming is not a
substitute for measurement or for the promotion gates.

tools.name: evolution_doctor
tools.description: Model-free health report for the Evolution bundle. Reads real package, host, registration, data, state, migration, and promotion facts; distinguishes ok, degraded, and blocked with per-check evidence. Set repair=true only to apply repairs the report marks safe and idempotent (a restart is required for promotion-journal rollback and is never attempted against a live composition).

repair.description: Apply the repairs the report marks safe, then re-verify. Defaults to false (read-only).

composition.description: Also dump the composed profile through the official CLI (default true).

tools.name: evolution_history
tools.description: Read bounded non-sensitive domain history metadata, counts, and independent metric integration status. Pass query to get bounded on-demand experience recall (already-resolved problems, approaches that already failed, measured candidate strategies) instead of raw rows.

query.description: Optional problem/target text to recall directly relevant bounded experience for.

target.description: Optional evolution target used with query to detect an exact replay of prior work.

impactScope.description: Optional proposal impact scope used with query.

tools.name: evolution_maintain
tools.description: Reclaim disk space from history that is already absorbed: retire terminal archive records into aggregate rows (deleting the sealed segments they replaced) and discard the consumed prefix of the authenticated event log, pruning its markers behind a durable retention floor. Promotion and measurement evidence is externalized before the log prefix is discarded. Everything is verified: unreadable or conflicting archive evidence, a pending transaction, an unreadable log, or a log that changed during planning aborts the whole call without discarding anything. dryRun reports the exact counts and bytes without modifying anything; a real call requires confirmation: true.

dryRun.description: Report the archive and log reclaim a real call would perform, without changing anything.

confirmation.description: Required for a real reclaim; the operation deletes committed archive segments and authenticated log bytes.

log.description: Discard the absorbed event log prefix and prune its markers (default true).

retainRecords.description: How many of the newest absorbed log records to keep in the log (default 1024, minimum 1).

tools.name: evolution_runtime_inspect
tools.description: Inspect the live Cordis Runtime. Returns facts from Cordis registries and scoped services; it does not use a static Evolution inventory.

tools.name: evolution_propose
tools.description: Create an owned Evolution Proposal before changing the Cordis composition.

risk.description: low, medium, or high; autonomous execution only accepts low.

tools.name: evolution_trial
tools.description: Define and activate a temporary Cordis Package for an existing Evolution Proposal. The Host Runner owns its Fiber and lifecycle.

idPrefix.description: Optional 3–6 lowercase semantic prefix for the Host-minted dynamic Plugin ID.

tools.name: evolution_measure
tools.description: Record an Observation for a running Evolution Trial and evaluate the Promotion gates.

beforeMetrics.description: Baseline metrics captured before the Trial.

afterMetrics.description: Metrics captured after the Trial observation window.

sampleCount.description: Positive number of samples represented by afterMetrics.

tools.name: evolution_revert
tools.description: Stop and undefine a temporary Evolution Plugin through Cordis, then prove the Runtime signature returned to its baseline.

tools.name: evolution_promote
tools.description: Prepare, apply, and verify a measured Trial as a durable Cordis Plugin, then enter canary observation. Stable commit requires deterministic startup/health/dependency/metric barriers. Set confirmation=true only after reviewing the measured evidence and rollback proof; false or omitted returns an owner-confirmation result without mutating production.

confirmation.description: Explicit owner confirmation for production promotion. Only true authorizes the promotion; false or omitted is a read-only confirmation request.

tools.name: evolution_canary_observe
tools.description: Advance a pending promotion canary at a deterministic barrier. Startup, component health, dependencies, and metrics must remain healthy; regression automatically rolls back.

degradedCapabilities.impact: The domain evaluator records a decision and hard-vetoes a detected regression, but promotionGates remains the production authority; independent host baseline/test metrics are not wired in.
degradedCapabilities.resolution: Provide a DSH host surface that supplies independent baseline/test metrics for an experiment.

degradedCapabilities.impact: lib/dockyard-domain/continuous and lib/dockyard-domain/governance are pure domain modules covered by unit tests and are not started by the orchestrator live loop.
degradedCapabilities.resolution: Wire them into the live loop behind an explicit opt-in once the loop is designed.

degradedCapabilities.impact: Client halves are rejected; promoted host code runs through a cooperative Function(hostCode)() gate that is not a security sandbox.
degradedCapabilities.resolution: Requires an approval-aware durable composition contract from the host.

degradedCapabilities.impact: lib/compat/legacy-startup-drift.js and the legacy preset/default-path handling stay present but disabled by default.
degradedCapabilities.resolution: Remove once no supported DSH layout publishes the legacy drift engine or preset layout.

degradedCapabilities.impact: Two introspection surfaces are private to Cordis by its own rule: ctx.events._hooks (no public listener enumeration exists) and the ctx.reflect._getImpl() fallback (used only when the documented ctx.reflect.store + Context.isolate path is absent). FiberState.ACTIVE is not importable (const enum, erased at runtime), so ACTIVE is decided from documented lifecycle fields. The official loader/Include members used for the mounted promoted row (EntryTree.resolve/root, Entry.fiber/options/disabled) are public but undocumented.
degradedCapabilities.resolution: Replace ctx.events._hooks once the host publishes a public listener enumeration; every other surface already goes through a documented or explicitly classified path recorded in lib/cordis-compat.js.
